name: Pirc Defense
summary: The Pirc (…d6, …Nf6, …g6) lets White build a broad centre, then strikes at it with a fianchettoed bishop.
intro: The Pirc Defense, 1.e4 d6 2.d4 Nf6 3.Nc3 g6, is a hypermodern system in which Black cedes the centre to attack it later. The bishop on g7 and timely breaks with ...e5 or ...c5 give Black flexible, counterattacking play.
line: e4 d6 d4 Nf6 Nc3 g6

sections.heading: Strategic ideas
paragraphs: The Pirc Defense is a hypermodern system in which Black allows White a broad pawn centre and prepares to challenge it from a distance. After 1.e4 d6 2.d4 Nf6 3.Nc3 g6 Black fianchettoes the king's bishop to g7, aiming it along the long diagonal at White's centre and queenside. Rather than staking a claim in the centre with pawns, Black develops flexibly and waits to strike back with the freeing breaks ...e5 or ...c5.

This approach cedes space in return for a resilient, elastic position with many piece-play possibilities. Black typically castles kingside early and keeps options open, choosing the moment and the manner of the central counter based on White's setup. The trade-off is that if Black delays too long, White's space advantage can grow into a dangerous initiative.

sections.heading: Main variations
paragraphs: White's most aggressive try is the Austrian Attack with f4, building an imposing pawn front of e4, d4 and f4 and often castling kingside with attacking intentions. The Classical System with Nf3 is more restrained, developing naturally and keeping a healthy space edge. The 150 Attack, featuring Be3, Qd2 and f3 with ideas of Bh6 and a kingside pawn storm, has become a popular and direct way to challenge the Pirc.

Against each setup Black relies on the same toolkit: complete the fianchetto, castle, and time the ...e5 or ...c5 break to contest the centre. The choice between these breaks depends on White's structure; ...e5 challenges the d4 pawn head-on, while ...c5 pressures d4 from the side and can open the c-file for counterplay.

keyIdeas: Black cedes the centre and fianchettoes the bishop to g7
The freeing breaks ...e5 and ...c5 are the heart of Black's counterplay
Flexible, hypermodern development lets Black react to White's setup
Early kingside castling gives a compact, resilient position
White's space can become an attack if Black delays the counter too long
The g7-bishop pressures the long diagonal against d4 and the queenside

white: Build a broad centre with e4 and d4 and expand for a space advantage
Launch the Austrian Attack with f4 and a kingside pawn storm
Play the Classical System with Nf3 for solid, natural development
Adopt the 150 Attack with Be3, Qd2 and f3, targeting g7 with Bh6
Restrain Black's ...e5 and ...c5 breaks while increasing pressure
black: Fianchetto the bishop to g7 and castle kingside quickly
Prepare and time the ...e5 break to challenge d4 directly
Use the ...c5 break to pressure d4 and open the c-file
Develop flexibly and choose the plan based on White's chosen setup
Exploit the long diagonal and any overextension in White's centre
